boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Farmville corridors within Hampden-Sydney College’s practical driving orbit, each paired with one verified reason to stop.

cards.title: Read the Student Strike Story
cards.subtitle: Griffin Boulevard at South Main Street
cards.notes: Follow Griffin Boulevard to the former Moton High School, then explore the classrooms and exhibits documenting Farmville’s student-led civil-rights history.
cards.short_summary: A historic school building preserves the story of the 1951 student walkout.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is at 900 Griffin Boulevard, offers free general admission, and presents civil-rights education and Virginia history.
cards.access_notes: Guest hours are noon–4 p.m. Monday–Saturday and by appointment; onsite parking is limited.

cards.entity_name: Longwood Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Step Into the Downtown Galleries
cards.subtitle: North Main Street at East Third Street
cards.notes: Pause at the Main-and-Third corner for the current exhibitions; consult the museum calendar first if a particular show prompted your trip.
cards.short_summary: Free university galleries anchor one of downtown Farmville’s most visible corners.
cards.evidence_claim: LCVA is located at 129 North Main Street at the intersection of Third and Main streets, and admission is free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Visit - Longwood Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; closed Monday and holidays.

cards.entity_name: High Bridge Trail State Park — Main Street Plaza
cards.title: Join the Rail Trail Downtown
cards.subtitle: North Main Street at the High Bridge Trail corridor
cards.notes: Enter at the downtown Main Street plaza for the westbound trail; review the park alert before riding toward High Bridge while bridge work affects the eastern segment.
cards.short_summary: The state rail trail crosses Main Street in downtown Farmville.
cards.evidence_claim: Virginia State Parks lists municipal-lot trail access where High Bridge Trail intersects Main Street in Farmville and identifies the Main Street plaza as a trip starting point.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are dawn–dusk. Check current alerts: River Road bridge work has affected the trail east of Main Street.

cards.title: Collect a Local Map First
cards.subtitle: East Third Street corridor
cards.notes: Start at 121 East Third Street to collect regional information before choosing a museum, trail, or historic stop elsewhere in Farmville and Prince Edward County.
cards.short_summary: A staffed information stop helps orient a wider Farmville outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Virginia’s Heartland Regional Visitor Center is located at 121 East Third Street in Farmville.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Saturday 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed Sunday and specified holidays.

cards.title: Settle In With a Book or Program
cards.subtitle: West Third Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue along West Third Street to browse the library or check its event calendar for writing, craft, and educational programs before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: The regional library adds a quiet public destination to the West Third Street run.
cards.evidence_claim: Central Virginia Regional Library identifies its Farmville Library venue at 1303 West Third Street and lists public programs there.
cards.source_title: Farmville Library | Central Virginia Regional Library
cards.access_notes: Program times vary; consult the library’s current event listing before visiting for a specific activity.

cards.title: Take a Lakeside Break
cards.subtitle: West Third Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow West Third Street to the lake for a picnic or field activity; respect the closed playground notice and bring a Virginia license if you plan to fish.
cards.short_summary: A free town park provides lake views, picnic tables, and open grass beside West Third Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The town places Wilck’s Lake Park on West Third Street, describes picnic tables and a grassy field, and states that the area is free to residents and visitors.
cards.access_notes: Open year-round dawn–dusk. The playground is currently closed; public fishing requires a valid Virginia fishing license.

cards.title: Catch Saturday Market Hours
cards.subtitle: North Street corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto North Street on a scheduled Saturday to browse produce, baked goods, meats, and crafts inside the town’s open-air marketplace building.
cards.short_summary: A former tobacco warehouse hosts Farmville’s seasonal community market.
cards.evidence_claim: The town identifies the Farmville Community Marketplace at 213 North Street and says the farmers market offers local produce, meats, baked goods, and handcrafted goods.
cards.access_notes: Regular market: Saturdays 9 a.m.–1 p.m. from the first Saturday in April through the Saturday before Thanksgiving; winter dates differ.

cards.title: Arrange a Trail Bike
cards.subtitle: 318 North Main Street, near Depot Street
cards.notes: Stop on North Main Street to arrange a bike rental or ask about repairs before entering the nearby High Bridge Trail; confirm winter availability in advance.
cards.short_summary: A downtown outfitter connects North Main Street with the adjacent rail-trail experience.
cards.evidence_claim: The store’s official page lists 318 North Main Street and offers bicycle rentals, repairs, parts, gear, and merchandise.
cards.source_title: About Our Store - Sandy River Outdoor Adventures
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; January–February hours are limited.

cards.title: Browse the Paddling Showroom
cards.subtitle: 614 North Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue north to inspect canoes, kayaks, and paddling equipment in person; contact the showroom before traveling if you need a particular model or service.
cards.short_summary: A specialist paddlesports showroom gives upper North Main Street a practical outdoor focus.
cards.evidence_claim: Appomattox River Company’s official site lists its Farmville location at 614 North Main Street and describes it as a canoe and kayak specialty store.
cards.access_notes: Contact the business directly for current showroom hours and product availability.

cards.title: Check the Workshop Calendar
cards.subtitle: 104 North Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for the red door on North Main Street, then consult the studio schedule for an arts or crafts class that matches your date and experience level.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown studio provides a hands-on arts stop on North Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Farmville identifies Red Door 104 at 104 North Main Street and says it offers arts-and-crafts workshops and classes.
cards.access_notes: Workshop schedules and participation costs vary; verify the current calendar with the studio before visiting.
